required_changes.change: Make structural-symbol genuinely complete: individually list, or give an exact finite lexical membership rule covering, every keyword, operator, delimiter, and type token usable in source. At minimum cover SPEAKER, USER, AGENT, REPLY_TO, REVISES, DECREASES, ANY, ALL, SATISFIES, ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, ->, =, :, parentheses, braces, brackets, commas, and the lexical delimiters/prefixes used by literals. Restore utterance to step (or define distinct task_step and turn_step productions) so a CONVO TURN can contain UTTER as required by Utterance and Conversation. Revalidate and correct every Conversation and Utterance worked example after this change.

Define one canonical opaque-handle allocation rule, such as preorder introduction order $v1, $v2, ..., and require it for entrypoints, tasks, turns, parameters, results, and loop variables. The current HANDLE regex accepts arbitrary semantically suggestive spellings and prevents deterministic encoding.

Add a canonical construct-selection/planning rule that determines when a request is encoded as TASK/GENERATE versus CONVO/UTTER and, for common closed task patterns, determines canonical decomposition rather than allowing equivalent find-and-loop and repeated-action plans.

Add a non-prose, recursively structured CODE/PROGRAM category sufficient to encode source-language tokens, calls, assignment, lists, expected/actual outputs, configuration mappings, commands, and assertions. Define typed symbolic syntax-tree constructs and vocabulary categories rather than a quoted code string; this is required to cover SWE-bench without violating N4.

Define valid literal lexical forms completely: specify calendar validity for DATE_LITERAL, ranges for TIME_LITERAL, URL grammar/boundaries, PATH normalization, NAME normalization/casing, and whether lexical productions are mutually exclusive. Also define the static type of ontology symbols and constrain ontology_symbol so an operation symbol cannot be passed wherever an arbitrary value is accepted.

Replace the removal of CONTEXT with a glossary-defined, typed translation-anchor mechanism for resolving relative dates, or require relative dates to be rejected unless a DATE/TIME anchor is supplied. The current proposal cannot deterministically translate 'Friday' while preserving auditable source meaning.

logic_issues: N1 is not realized: structural-symbol is declared closed but omits numerous source tokens used by grammar and examples, and its null membership_rule does not define the omitted tokens.
Conversation is broken because revised Task.step excludes utterance, while turn ::= ... { step+ } and Utterance requires legal placement inside a CONVO TURN body.
The Conversation worked examples use SPEAKER and USER, neither of which is a listed structural-symbol member.

The claim that every ontology symbol matches exactly one category is not enforced by the grammar: ontology_symbol alternatives and attribute-symbol's unrestricted lowercase lexical form can overlap without a global prefix/reserved-word disjointness rule.
HANDLE suffixes are claimed opaque but remain arbitrary source tokens; absent a canonical allocation rule, equivalent expressions can differ in every binding name.
The proposal asserts canonical attribute order but supplies no actual schemas for the shown operation and intent members; the examples depend on unshown signatures.
The Types & Lexicon worked example uses recipient, duration, unit, and tone but does not establish their allowed parent/schema rules in the supplied entries.
No representational category exists for program/configuration syntax and exact multi-token outputs, producing a genuine closed-domain coverage failure for SWE-bench.
critic_reasoning: The central idea—replace free text with typed literals, glossary categories, and recursive propositions—is a positive direction and removes the prior direct prose violations. It cannot be accepted because N1 remains hard-violated by an incomplete structural vocabulary, and the Task revision makes all UTTER-containing conversations grammatically invalid. The proposal also leaves deterministic handle allocation and canonical plan selection unresolved and lacks a symbolic code representation needed for sampled closed SWE-bench tasks.

N1.reasoning: The proposal removes STRING and free identifiers, but its own grammar and examples use structural source tokens not defined as structural-symbol members or produced by a precise glossary rule. In particular SPEAKER, USER, AGENT, REPLY_TO, REVISES, DECREASES, ANY, ALL, SATISFIES, punctuation delimiters, arrows, and comparison operators are not traceable through the supplied closed category.

N2.reasoning: The proposal makes substantial progress by adding descriptive vocabulary categories, membership rules, glosses, and examples. Yet the structural category is incomplete, operation and intent signatures are deferred rather than shown for the listed entries, and several word kinds used in examples have no complete glossary entry.

N3.reasoning: The semantic rule correctly requires attributes to be authorized by their parent signature and values to belong to defined categories or allowed types. However, the supplied glossary does not give the required per-intent and per-operation schemas/value sets for the displayed entries, so the rule cannot yet be checked from the glossary.

N4.reasoning: The revised grammar removes STRING and quoted payloads, and the simulated non-code expressions use only symbolic propositions, typed literals, ontology symbols, and handles. The missing code representation is a coverage failure, not a license to use prose.

N5.reasoning: Atomic DATE, TIME, URL, PATH, NAME, NUMBER, and HANDLE forms are a sound self-contained direction, and the proposal prohibits phrase syntax. But several literal-form boundaries and normalization rules remain underspecified, and incomplete structural-token definition means a reader cannot fully resolve source vocabulary using only the glossary.

N6.reasoning: The grammar is largely category-based and the simulations use assumed members of existing entity, role, operation, intent, attribute, and attribute-value categories rather than reshaping syntax around absent individual entries. The missing CODE category is correctly treated as a genuine category gap rather than a missing member.

N7.reasoning: Canonical attribute order is promised but not fully supplied, arbitrary handle spellings remain legal, and independent translations choose materially different plans and top-level constructs for equivalent requests. The broken turn grammar additionally prevents a unique valid parse/encoding for ordinary dialogue.

N8.reasoning: Recursive propositions preserve considerably more structure than prose payloads, including nested persona, tone, quantity, recipient, and ordering constraints. Richness is nevertheless lost for code-bearing tasks, and schemas must be concretely defined to avoid collapsing nuanced requests into broad uninspectable intent symbols.

logic_issues: Doc hygiene failed because three claimed vocabulary revisions target glossary entries that do not exist; therefore the categories that are supposed to establish N1 are not added at all.
The proposed grammar references undefined lexical nonterminals including POSITIVE_INTEGER, YYYY, MM, DD, HH, SS, URL_BODY, and PATH_BODY, so it does not define every token it admits.

The `code-form` grammar uses raw argument labels such as `callee`, `args`, `target`, `value`, `items`, `entries`, `tokens`, `expected`, and `actual`; none are structural symbols or namespace-valid attribute symbols.

The code-form membership rule says `code_id` and `code_text` are code nodes but the worked examples call them with parentheses, while the grammar gives neither call syntax nor a production for those forms.
`@q` can encode an arbitrary natural-language sentence exactly, only hidden as hexadecimal code points. Calling decoded text data does not prevent it from being an N4-prohibited prose payload.

The proposal relies on a hypothetical complete glossary for most symbols used in its own examples (`int_plan_trip`, `attr_destination`, `ent_italy`, and many more), but does not add the referenced entity, role, value, or attribute categories to the actual glossary.

The canonical-operation rule is underdetermined because operation postconditions, identity behavior, and schemas are absent for the many operations required by the samples; independent provider disagreement confirms this is not a cosmetic issue.
The worked Types & Lexicon example says 'On 10 June 2025' but emits ANCHOR `@d2025-06-03`; this changes stated source information and the anchor has no explained relation to the date in the request.
critic_reasoning: This is a promising attempt to replace free strings with typed symbolic categories, and it addresses several prior rework requests conceptually. It cannot be accepted because doc hygiene failed and the resulting glossary does not actually contain the vocabulary that N1 requires; additionally, undefined lexical forms and hexadecimal prose-bearing code text independently violate hard N1, N4, and N5. The Shaper should repair the concrete glossary and grammar gaps, then demonstrate full symbolic SWE-bench encodings without `@q` prose smuggling.

N1.reasoning: The hard closed-vocabulary requirement is not met: the vocabulary additions failed hygiene and therefore do not exist in the glossary, multiple lexical productions use undefined metavariables, and code-form introduces unglossed raw labels. A reader cannot trace every token in the simulations to the supplied glossary or a fully defined glossary rule.

N2.reasoning: The actual glossary remains one-entry-per-construct and lacks the proposed descriptive Vocabulary section. Entity, role, value, and attribute categories are asserted in grammar but are neither added nor described with members, rules, and worked examples.

N3.reasoning: Schemas broadly accept `VALUE`, but individual attributes do not list their allowed value sets or an exact derivation rule. This permits undefined values and does not make attribute-value choice traceable.

N4.reasoning: `code_text(@q...)` permits arbitrary decoded natural-language text to be embedded in an expression, and the proposal supplies no symbolic schema capable of replacing detailed bug reports and other prose substance. Hexadecimal wrapping does not make a sentence non-prose for this constraint.

N5.reasoning: The URL rule delegates acceptance to RFC-3986 rather than defining it in the language/glossary, and `@q` admits arbitrary codepoint sequences whose interpretation can depend on external language/code syntax. The language is therefore not self-contained in the required sense.

required_changes.change: Remove COMMENT from BrainCode source or constrain comments so they cannot contain arbitrary natural-language text; N4 forbids the current `COMMENT ::= "--" [^\n]*` prose channel. Replace the URL semantic dependency on RFC-3986 with a complete in-spec lexical and validity grammar, and define all character-set/complement and newline semantics used by lexical productions.

Change every open-category membership rule from prefix-only acceptance to: valid exactly when a corresponding member entry exists in the complete glossary. A spelling such as `role_unlisted` or `int_unlisted` must not be a legal expression token merely because it matches a regex.

Implement N3: for every attribute, list its allowed value symbols/categories and any compositional rule, not merely the broad type VALUE. In particular define closed/permitted sets for tone, unit, ordering, currency, state, quality, goal, format, requirements, and failure values; reject values from an unrelated VALUE subcategory.

Give every operation and intent an actual complete ordered schema: required and optional attributes, their precise types/category restrictions, result type selection, duplicate/default behavior, and canonical selection/decomposition rules. Add a rule resolving `op_find`'s REF versus LIST result and define canonical ordering for all intent attributes.

Add schemas required by the closed samples: `op_add_to_cart`; acquisition/pick-up and removal/retrieval operations; compatible-with/reference constraints for product selection; and the web/household navigation or state transitions needed to make those actions executable. Specify when a source-location find is sufficient versus acquisition is required.

Replace the seven-node generic code subset with a typed, closed code AST sufficient for sampled issue facts: ordered statement sequences, imports, member/attribute access, indexing/bracket calls versus parenthesized calls, lists/tuples/dictionaries, typed string atoms, URLs/status assertions, file edits, tests, expected/actual behavior, and regression criteria. Give `int_bug_report` a complete schema whose reproduction field accepts the appropriate typed code sequence. Demonstrate full valid symbolic encodings for both sampled SWE-bench reports.

Add compositional symbolic schemas/categories for the missing open-task content rather than treating it as opaque prose: recipes and nutrient/review/time constraints; recommendations with proximity/conditions; opinions and historical explanations; technical explanation and persona/register composition; scripts, cast, scene, humor and rating; sermons and ordered instructional guidance; email-generation and generated reply relations; CRUD design alternatives; meal plans; and medical explanations/prognosis with audience-age constraints.

Define a canonical representation for conversational requests versus requested generated artifacts, plus references to previously generated artifacts and follow-up questions. It must encode c5957's revision, nutrition question, and time question without prose, and remove the current Task-versus-CONVO ambiguity shown by the independent translations.

Revalidate every worked example against the revised grammar and schemas. In particular, ensure generated target symbols have a declared value entry, operation result types match their schemas, and no example relies on an intent attribute (`attr_tone` on `int_follow_up`, `attr_destination` on `int_plan_trip`) that its intent schema has not defined.

logic_issues: N1 is still violated because role, value, attribute, operation, and intent membership rules accept any namespace-shaped token without requiring a corresponding glossary entry.
N4 is violated by arbitrary COMMENT text, which is a direct natural-language channel inside a source expression.
N3 is violated because attributes typed VALUE accept the undifferentiated open value category; the proposal does not list admissible values or a derivation rule per attribute.
The URL semantic requirement delegates validity to RFC-3986, contradicting N5's requirement that reading BrainCode not depend on an external natural-language standard.
`op_find` promises `LIST[REF[ENTITY]] or REF[ENTITY]` without a type-selection rule, leaving valid encodings and subsequent typechecking indeterminate.
Most intent entries name a meaning but provide no schema at all, despite the grammar allowing arbitrary listed attributes. This creates both under-expression and multiple competing encodings.

The code-form example uses `int_bug_report` as a code-change payload, but bug-report schemas do not define that as a patch/change representation; generic code_call also cannot distinguish the critical Mathematica syntactic forms.

The proposed lexical grammar says ontology categories are namespace-disjoint, but the structural glossary aggregates multiple punctuation tokens as single members and does not define a per-token lookup rule for those grouped entries.
critic_reasoning: The attempt addresses several prior structural requests and passes doc hygiene, but it cannot be accepted because hard notes N1 through N5 and N7 remain violated. In particular, prefix-only namespace rules and unrestricted comments prevent a genuinely closed, prose-free vocabulary, while generic VALUE and incomplete schemas leave encoding non-canonical. The core direction is sound, so the appropriate decision is needs-rework rather than rejection.

N1.reasoning: The proposal makes substantial progress by adding namespaces, literal forms, and structural symbols, but prefix-only membership rules for role/value/attribute/operation/intent symbols permit tokens absent from the glossary. A direct arbitrary-prose COMMENT production is also legal. Therefore a reader cannot trace every source token to a glossary member or glossary-defined closed production.

N2.reasoning: Descriptive categories were added, which is progress, but they do not provide a complete lexicon in the required sense: broad prefix rules stand in for actual members, many necessary categories are absent, and most operation/intent entries lack complete schemas and examples of their descriptive relations.

N3.reasoning: The attribute entries state coarse static types such as VALUE, but they do not give each attribute its permissible value set or a precise derivation rule. Consequently `val_comedy` is formally admissible as a tone, unit, or currency despite not being meaningful.

N4.reasoning: The language removes STRING and quoted text, but unrestricted comment text remains legal in source. In addition, most substantive sampled requests cannot be symbolically encoded, demonstrating that the replacement ontology is not yet sufficient for the no-prose requirement.

N5.reasoning: URL validity is defined by reference to RFC-3986 rather than fully by BrainCode's own specification. Prefix-only ontology admission also leaves symbol meaning dependent on an alleged external complete glossary entry that need not exist.

N6.reasoning: The syntax is now mostly written over categories and simulations appropriately assume missing entities such as toilet paper can belong to a complete entity glossary. However, many failures are missing categories/schemas, not merely missing members, and the categories are not closed by actual glossary membership.

N7.reasoning: The handle rule is helpful, but canonical encoding is not achieved: `op_find` result cardinality is unspecified, intent schemas and argument order are absent, and independent translations diverge substantially on plan shape and construct selection.

N8.reasoning: Structured literals and code nodes attempt to retain richness, but the current ontology is too coarse for the sampled open requests and too weak for both SWE reports. The necessary response is richer compositional symbolic schemas, not restoration of prose payloads.

coverage.reasoning: The complete-glossary contract, typed propositions, symbolic code trees, and new household/cart operations materially improve coverage without prose for the sampled domains. However, the explicitly supplied operation and intent schemas remain far narrower than the current Action vocabulary, and several required domains are only asserted to exist in an unspecified future complete glossary; the revised grammar does not yet provide a complete executable basis for them.

expressivity.reasoning: The proposal can structurally encode quantities, ordering, compatibility, date constraints, revisions, follow-up questions, code-tree facts, generated artifacts, and many conversational constraints that were formerly hidden in strings. It still loses or leaves unspecified important distinctions such as exact artifact content, persona composition, source-code literal values, medical qualification, and many detailed travel, meal, and sermon constraints because the corresponding schemas are not actually defined.

determinism.reasoning: Opaque canonical handles, canonical field order, exact glossary membership, and explicit Check precedence are strong improvements. But the duplicate, materially different Generate revisions conflict; schemas do not consistently define selection/decomposition rules; and independent translations diverged substantially on possession handling, price constraints, bug-report attributes, and whether an open request is TASK/CONVO/GENERATE.

interpretability.reasoning: Replacing arbitrary identifiers and prose payloads with typed handles and named ontology symbols improves inspectability. The basis is nevertheless difficult to interpret because the proposal repeatedly delegates decisive schemas and vocabulary to an unshown “complete glossary,” several symbols used in examples lack supplied entries, and two incompatible Generate definitions appear in one change set.

improvement.reasoning: For executable tasks, explicit data flow, typed references, operation schemas, structured conditions, and symbolic conversational links would help a weaker agent plan more reliably than raw requests. The benefit is limited for complex open and software tasks until the promised schemas are made concrete enough to determine what action or artifact structure is required.

The Types & Lexicon worked example calls int_request_extension without its schema-required attr_recipient field.

The ontology membership rule promises exact glossary membership but does not provide the actual category entries, schemas, or canonical mappings necessary to verify most sampled symbols.

The code_atom gloss calls code atoms “string atom” while N4 forbids natural-language fragments; without a precise atomic subtype grammar and exact-entry discipline this is an unclear prose re-entry channel.
Conversation confines TURN bodies to UTTER, while generated-artifact requests require GENERATE; no legal connection is defined between the conversational request and requested generation.
critic_reasoning: This is a sound and substantial move toward the closed symbolic vocabulary required by N1: it eliminates the largest free-text and free-identifier channels while adding typed literals, handles, exact-membership rules, and structured values. It cannot be accepted because two incompatible Generate revisions leave the grammar ambiguous, multiple worked examples violate their own schemas, and most claimed closed vocabulary is only promised rather than supplied in usable category schemas. Fixing those concrete issues would preserve the strong N1 progress while materially improving determinism and interpretability.

N1.reasoning: The removal of STRING, comments, unrestricted IDENT, and prefix-only namespace acceptance is real progress, and literal forms plus canonical handles are substantially better defined. N1 is not yet upheld because many symbols needed for valid expressions are delegated to an unspecified complete glossary rather than being traceable in the supplied glossary/category entries, and the conflicting Generate definitions prevent a reader from determining the final legal source language.

N2.reasoning: The added structural-symbol and ontology-symbol categories are a major move beyond one construct entry per glossary item. The glossary still does not actually contain the full descriptive lexicon, its category members, value sets, and worked examples required for the many asserted domains.

N3.reasoning: Several operation and intent entries now name narrow value subcategories such as duration-unit, tone-value, currency-value, and nutrient-value, rather than accepting generic VALUE. Numerous attributes used by schemas and examples have no own glossary entries or permitted values, and the claimed remaining subcategories are not enumerated or defined.

N4.reasoning: The proposed source syntax removes quoted strings, comments, and free-text payloads, and simulations use only structural symbols, literals, handles, and ontology/code symbols. This status depends on enforcing the proposal's exact-entry rule for code_atom and ontology entries; the ambiguous “string atom” wording must be tightened to avoid reopening a prose channel.

N5.reasoning: Atomic NUMBER, DATE, TIME, URL, PATH, NAME, and opaque-handle forms are explicitly constrained, while descriptive tokens are intended to acquire meaning only through exact glossary entries. The literal and handle rules are a meaningful self-contained improvement over English-derived identifiers and strings.

N6.reasoning: The grammar is now stated over ontology categories and the simulations may assume a complete glossary within established categories. However, many needed categories themselves remain only an assertion in a membership-rule paragraph rather than defined compositional categories, so translators cannot reliably tell whether a missing symbol belongs to an existing category or represents a language gap.

N7.reasoning: Canonical handles, ordered fields, duplicate rejection, fixed Check precedence, and exact symbol membership improve encoding determinism. The duplicate Generate definitions, missing canonical decomposition/selection rules for many domains, and low independent-translator agreement mean one canonical expression per meaning is not yet achieved.

N8.reasoning: Typed propositions and code trees seek to retain substantially more structure than opaque prose, including quantities, relations, branches, and revisions. Richness remains aspirational for most open domains because their schemas are neither concrete nor compositional enough to preserve detailed meaning.

coverage.reasoning: The closed symbolic basis improves representability for a narrow set of household, email, recipe, and simple recommendation tasks, but removes the current language's ability to retain the actionable core of most sampled web, SWE-bench, planning, and open-generation tasks. Missing operations and schemas include sorting/filtering, rinsing/slicing, code bug reports and arbitrary structured edits, legal documents, channel schedules, mortgage advice, and story generation.

expressivity.reasoning: Typed propositions, dates, paths, quantities, handles, and revision links preserve more structure than prior strings where a supplied schema fits. However, most sample meanings cannot be represented without omitting essential relations, constraints, requested artifact form, or substantive content; under N4 those omissions are failures rather than permissible opaque payloads.

determinism.reasoning: Canonical handles, ordered schema fields, typed values, and an explicit structural vocabulary materially reduce prior identifier and string variation. Determinism remains incomplete because the ontology does not define canonical construct selection for many meanings and providers disagree on operation/field choice, such as source versus location, recommendations versus explain requests, and unsupported code edits.

interpretability.reasoning: Closed literal forms and typed schemas are easier to inspect than free strings, and the revised grammar distinguishes source notation from source tokens. But densely grouped glossary entries obscure individual attribute/category meanings, schemas omit many needed concepts, and the claimed complete ontology is not actually published, so a reader cannot recover omitted task meaning from many expressions.

improvement.reasoning: For supported operational tasks, explicit find/pick-up/place sequencing and typed conversational propositions would aid a weaker agent. For unsupported tasks, the only legal approximation loses the requested work, so the expression would make an agent worse than the original request.

logic_issues: The ontology entry calls its listed value symbols 'Exact members' while multiple required artifact and semantic categories have no member or schema; the future-member rule does not make an absent artifact specification legal today.
op_find's a_requirement accepts only PROPOSITION, but no supplied proposition schema expresses high rating, comedy genre, audience-score ordering, or similar common search constraints.

The current grouped attribute list is not independently lookupable per attribute or value category, so it does not fully satisfy the prior required change or N2's glossary organization requirement.
critic_reasoning: This attempt makes substantial, sound progress on the focus note by closing free-text and free-identifier channels, so N1 is now upheld in the grammar. It cannot be accepted because the narrow replacement ontology causes broad coverage and richness regressions, including most sampled open tasks and both SWE-bench fixes, and because several previously required concrete schema additions remain incomplete. The core direction is sound, but the next revision must expand closed symbolic composition rather than rely on unsupported approximations.

N1.reasoning: The revised grammar eliminates STRING, unrestricted IDENT, comments, and quoted payloads; source positions are structural symbols, exact ontology members, atomic literals, or canonical handles. Subject to N6's stipulated complete-glossary assumption, every token in the supported simulations has a glossary entry or a glossary-defined production rule.

N2.reasoning: Structural and ontology vocabulary categories are newly added and substantially improve on the construct-only glossary. However, entity, role, and value categories are largely asserted rather than independently enumerated or separately lookupable, and significant descriptive domains remain absent.

N3.reasoning: Fields now require typed literals, handles, proposition trees, code trees, or ontology symbols, and schemas state allowed categories. The remaining problem is insufficient category richness, not an unrestricted attribute-value channel.

N4.reasoning: The revised productions exclude quoted text and prose payloads, and all descriptive content must occur as symbolic proposition/code structure or atomic literals. This is real progress despite the substantial missing ontology needed to encode many requests.

N5.reasoning: Literal forms are explicitly atomic and locally defined, while descriptive symbols require exact glossary membership. No expression production depends on English sentence grammar.

N6.reasoning: The grammar now targets ontology categories and the simulations appropriately assume entity members within an existing entity category. It remains partial because several required categories and compositional schemas do not exist at all; N6 cannot cure missing categories.

N7.reasoning: Fixed field order, handle allocation, typing, and precedence substantially improve encoding discipline. Independent translations still diverge over available fields and construct choices, and canonical mappings for many meanings are not supplied.

N8.reasoning: The supported subset gains useful typed richness, but compared with the current prose-capable language, most sampled requests now lose their core content or constraints outright. The necessary N4 closure must be accompanied by a much broader symbolic ontology rather than a collapse to a few coarse schemas.

coverage.reasoning: The proposal adds useful symbolic coverage for rinse/place, retrieval/filter/sort, artifact requests, and limited code ASTs. However, several sampled closed tasks still have no operation or proposition schema (file age/deletion/archive membership, selecting a nearest store, transit schedules, movable containers), and most open substantive requests remain unrepresentable without inventing ontology schemas.

expressivity.reasoning: Structured propositions improve preservation of recipients, durations, ranking, and some artifact constraints. But the schemas omit essential distinctions such as email drafting versus sending, file deletion, ZIP-based proximity, colors, containment, route endpoints, revisions of supplied tables, advice constraints, and most narrative/script content; several expressions therefore cannot preserve the request.

determinism.reasoning: The proposed canonical retrieval pipeline is beneficial locally, but the language does not define operation_symbol, intent_symbol, attribute_symbol, or the category-selection rules needed to select among schemas. Independent translations already diverge materially: for the red-rag task one uses a missing red entity while another uses filter/property; for the game comparison one omits versus includes a criterion; and both providers leave major gaps for code, store, and story tasks.

Yet the glossary combines dozens of supposedly independently lookupable attributes, values, operations, and schemas into bulk entries, leaves source categories and structural tokens undefined, and gives many values only an aspirational subtype statement rather than a usable per-symbol definition.

For many other tasks the model must either fail, invent undocumented symbols, or reduce the request to a vague explain/generate proposition, which does not improve planning over the original request.

logic_issues: The grammar uses operation_symbol, intent_symbol, attribute_symbol, code_constructor, and speaker-related categories without defining productions that connect them to glossary_symbol or a glossary category.
The structural-symbol vocabulary omits AND, OR, and NOT even though Check admits them as source tokens.
The revised semantic schemas use fields not listed in the attribute declaration, including a_deadline in op_check_replied.

The semantic-symbol entry groups many distinct symbols in one member declaration, contrary to its claim that symbols are individually lookupable and contrary to N2's per-category/per-member requirement.

The generic value grammar admits glossary_symbol without a grammar-level category/type restriction; the later statement that each schema fixes types is not a parseable or lookupable definition of each value category.
NAME_LITERAL permits arbitrary NAME_CHAR+ but NAME_CHAR is not defined, and the semantics do not mechanically restrict names to proper-name atoms rather than arbitrary English words.

The global preorder handle rule is incompatible or at least unspecified for ENTRYPOINT $v1 followed by TASK $v1: the first occurrence appears to use the handle before the declaration that introduces it.
Task calls and declaration handles have no declared task-signature registry or handle-to-task resolution procedure, so a HANDLE(...) step is not statically resolvable.
The proposal claims every schema fixes defaults, but no default values or default application rules are supplied.

Several worked examples rely on unlisted exact symbols, including ent_new_zealand_politics, ent_place, ent_netherlands, ent_japan, ent_sgi, val_objective_strength, and val_formal; N6 allows a complete glossary to contain members only after the category/subtype/consuming-schema rules are complete, which they are not here.
critic_reasoning: The revision makes genuine progress toward closed vocabulary by removing free strings and adding symbolic categories, so its core direction is sound. It cannot be accepted because key grammar categories and fixed tokens are still undefined, the glossary is not individually lookupable, and most sampled requests lack symbolic schemas under the no-prose constraint. N4.reasoning: STRING payloads remain intentionally available in this build phase, including subject, constraints, code expected/actual outputs, UTTER content, and generated artifact content. The proposal does not remove them, as N2 correctly instructs it not to do yet.

N5.reasoning: Although several atomic categories are proposed, the exact syntax of PATH, URL, CODE_SYMBOL, COMMAND, and ISO_DATE is not defined, and open underscore-word rules still rely on unbounded English-like token invention.

coverage.reasoning: The new operations improve coverage for transit searches, store selection, typed code-fix fields, and several household operations. expressivity.reasoning: Structured code fields, ranking fields, and typed date/path slots preserve more request structure than the current spec. determinism.reasoning: Canonical attribute ordering and the speech-act registry are genuine improvements. Determinism remains weak because the same search request can be represented either through named criteria or an opaque target/content STRING; category membership rules permit broad invented underscore identifiers; `UNSIGNED_INT_LIT` overlaps NUMBER lexically; and operation, task, turn, and attribute namespaces are still not comprehensively specified.

interpretability.reasoning: The structural-word, key-term, literal-form, search-criterion, code-structure, and speech-act indexes make much more of the language discoverable. The benefit is limited for generation and many conversational tasks because their central substance remains opaque STRING content.

required_changes.change: Retain and explicitly state the prior default-operation behavior, or add typed canonical operations for every previously expressible default operation. At minimum preserve offer_discount and offer_expedited_shipping so the held support task does not regress.

Add separate glossary categories for every Action/UTTER/GENERATE operation identifier and every attribute name, with member glosses, applicability, canonical synonyms, and worked examples. A signature inside the Action construct is not a descriptive glossary category and does not satisfy N2.

Add typed, canonical symbolic criteria and values for shape and availability/stock status, and state canonical precedence between dedicated search_web filters and select_filter/apply_filters so one meaning has one encoding.

Repair the literal and token audit: define PATH_LIT's segment and DRIVE subrules, list the actual '#' comment token rather than only COMMENT, define the complete identifier/handle formation rules for task, conversation, turn, variable, result, operation, and attribute positions, and remove or formally define all documentation-only comment notation before claiming an exhaustive lexicon.

Constrain source to location-provider (or a typed compatible REF), relation and destination_relation to spatial-relation, destination_location to location-provider, and each search parameter to its stated category in normative grammar/semantics rather than only prose claims.

Add an explicit glossary category or derivation rule for every currently accepted attribute and preserve STRING only as an explicitly labeled build-phase fallback. Cover recipient/audience roles, target kind, origin/location, content, format, constraints, deadline, subject, code fields, and all remaining search/action attributes; make tone slots normatively require tone-value.

Add the next increment of generation specification vocabulary: symbolic format, length/paragraph count, audience/recipient role, style, exclusion, locale, duration, and constraint categories, while retaining the transitional STRING fallback.

Add separately lookupable categories with applicability/composition rules. This is needed for the glossary's descriptive groups and for recipient/audience/source distinctions, although STRING fallback may remain during build phase.

logic_issues: The revised Action registry says it restores every previously supported operation but omits the current default signature for unlisted operations. This is a semantic coverage regression, not merely a missing glossary entry.
The structural-word category calls itself exhaustive but does not include the literal '#' comment marker, while the grammar defines COMMENT using '#'.
PATH_LIT references undefined lexical components DRIVE and segment; its POSIX and Windows recognition rule is therefore not fully self-contained.

location-provider's membership rule permits capitalized proper names but all listed symbols and IDENT syntax conventions are lowercase-oriented; the canonical case and proper-name encoding are not specified consistently.

descriptor-modifier is described as a closed-ish set, marked closed:false, and says membership is 'from this list, representative not exhaustive'; this does not provide a deterministic membership rule for unlisted values such as gray.

search-criterion conflates criterion names with their values and permits both structured search_web attributes and opaque apply_filters/select_filter content for overlapping filtering meanings, producing multiple valid encodings.
tone-value is added, but Action's send_email/send_message signatures still type tone as generic SYMBOL and the proposal does not normatively require a tone-value member.

The key-term worked example uses '-- lookup:' even though the revised lexical account declares '#' the only comment token; calling this documentation shorthand does not make an expression example parseable.
critic_reasoning: This is meaningful progress on N2: it fixes important lexical defects and adds useful descriptive categories that make several closed tasks expressible without prose. It cannot be accepted because the Action revision can remove previously available default operations, while the claimed complete glossary still omits operation and attribute vocabularies and retains concrete lexical inconsistencies. Fixing those issues would preserve the coverage gains and make this a sound accepted increment.

N2.reasoning: The attempt adds substantial structural, key-term, literal, entity, location, relation, descriptor, search, tone, and artifact glossary vocabulary. It remains incomplete because operation identifiers, attribute names, roles/recipients, providers, instance descriptors, and many semantic categories are not glossary categories; several claimed exhaustive categories are incomplete or undefined.

N3.reasoning: tone-value, spatial-relation, descriptor values, and some search value rules are genuine progress. Most existing attributes still accept arbitrary STRING or SYMBOL without an attribute-specific glossary value set or derivation rule; transitional STRING retention is allowed, but it does not satisfy N3.

N7.reasoning: Contextual UNSIGNED_INT, REPO_PATH, ordered rank fields, and namespace discussion improve canonical parsing and encoding. Competing structured versus content-string filters, open operation/speech-act selection, and missing canonical value mappings still prevent one encoding per meaning.

N1.reasoning: The attempt makes more tokens lookupable and removes COMMAND, but build-phase STRING and free identifiers remain by design. Moreover, operation and attribute identifiers remain unindexed, so the lexicon is not yet closed.

N4.reasoning: Numerous STRING payloads remain, but retaining them is required during this N2 build phase. The proposal neither removes nor expands such channels beyond the current language in a way that worsens this note.

N5.reasoning: Removing undefined COMMAND and formalizing REPO_PATH are sound self-containment progress. Undefined PATH components, arbitrary STRING payloads, and ungoverned identifier classes remain, so the language is not self-contained.

N6.reasoning: The categories are increasingly grammar-oriented and simulations appropriately assume missing members within entity/location categories. Missing categories for shape, availability, itinerary constraints, roles, and medical/legal concepts still force prose rather than category symbols.

N8.reasoning: Nested spatial relations, multi-key ranking, source, artifact kinds, and tone preserve useful distinctions. Shape, availability, code semantics, generation constraints, and recipient roles remain too coarse or opaque.

rebuttals.change: Add role-recipient, provider, instance-descriptor categories in this sprint.
rebuttals.argument: No simulated Fail-coverage item required role-recipient or instance-descriptor (only the Partial dev-email-1 touches recipient roles); every simulated Fail item (dev-embodied-2, both ALFRED items, both SWE-bench items) is fixed by the source/relation/entity/location/spatial-relation changes made this sprint. Adding two more categories now within the 12-change cap would force cutting one of those Fail-fixing changes, net-reducing coverage rather than improving it. Deferring keeps this step coherent and leaves no regression (STRING recipient remains usable under N2's build-phase carve-out).

rebuttals.change: Add all Action operation identifiers as their own descriptive vocabulary category (action-verb) this sprint.
rebuttals.argument: Every operation identifier is already enumerated, with its exact signature, inside the Action construct entry itself, so a reader can trace any operation token to a spec location today (no N1 regression). Promoting this into a separate glossary category is a valuable interpretability polish but adds no new expressible coverage and no simulated item was Failed by its absence; given the 12-change cap it is deferred to preserve room for the coverage-fixing changes above.

rebuttals.change: Add full generation-specification categories (character sheet, contract, structured report, invitation) with typed length/style/exclusion/locale attributes in this sprint.
rebuttals.argument: This sprint adds the artifact-type category itself (the prerequisite), covering story/story_continuation/technical_explanation/structured_report/character_description/email_reply/contract/list as a growable, closed:false set. Fully typing every generation attribute (paragraph counts, exclusions, locale, style) in the same sprint would be exactly the overreaching redesign the steering guidance warns against; it is scheduled for the next increment once artifact-type is validated against sampled items.

rebuttals.change: Give every attribute (tone, register_note, format, constraints, content, deadline, subject, origin, and all remaining STRING-typed attributes) an explicit category or derivation rule this sprint.
rebuttals.argument: N2's own build-phase text is explicit that free-text alternatives for these attributes are removed 'later, under N1 and N4' once the vocabulary is rich enough, and that this build phase must 'not remove STRING or other free-text channels' nor 'reduce coverage.' This sprint substantially grows that vocabulary (tone-value, descriptor-modifier, spatial-relation, artifact-type, expanded search-criterion, location-provider, entity-category) without yet retiring every STRING fallback, which is the correct sequencing under the note's own phasing; retiring all of them in one sprint risks exactly the coverage loss the note forbids.

rebuttal_rulings.reasoning: Deferring role-recipient and instance-descriptor for one increment is defensible under the build-phase incremental plan because STRING recipient fallback remains and the added source/relation categories repair more immediate closed-task failures. They remain required next-step N2 work.

N2 requires descriptive vocabulary categories in the glossary, not merely a list of operation names embedded in a construct grammar. The proposal itself claims operation identifiers belong in an action-vocabulary category, but supplies none; this leaves every operation word outside the claimed complete lexicon.

Adding artifact-type is real, coherent progress, and full generation-specification typing can be an immediately following increment without removing the required STRING fallback. The omitted generation categories remain required work, but not a reason to reject this increment by themselves.

The rebuttal correctly distinguishes retaining STRING fallback from closing it, but N3 explicitly requires every attribute to receive a value set or derivation rule during the build phase. A transitional STRING alternative may remain; it must still be named as such and cannot substitute for the missing symbolic value categories.

coverage.reasoning: The new household, search, support, role, entity, code-field, and generation categories materially improve coverage, and restoring the default Action rule avoids the prior support-task regression. However, sampled household requests still need semantic categories for state/instance descriptors and directional relations, while some search, code, and generation attributes have no indexed category.

expressivity.reasoning: Dedicated search criteria and generation facets preserve more request constraints than the prior all-STRING forms. But the language cannot distinguish the full versus empty toilet-paper rolls, cannot express left-of placement, and defines duration as a number whose unit is merely 'understood from context,' losing an explicit part of the source meaning.

determinism.reasoning: Canonical synonyms, typed criteria, and dedicated-filter precedence are real improvements. Yet the open default-operation membership rule depends on deciding whether a listed operation 'covers the same concept,' generic IDENT attributes remain grammatically admitted, and independent translations still diverge materially on support control flow, string versus symbols, temporal deal filtering, and target identity.

interpretability.reasoning: Separate glossary categories make many formerly implicit words look-upable. Interpretability is harmed by the false claim that attribute-name indexes every usable attribute, the undefined category(...) expression in the search example, and categories such as tone-value and artifact-type being required without an accompanying supplied glossary entry.

improvement.reasoning: Typed availability, shape, roles, locations, operations, code fields, and generation formats give a weaker executor materially better planning information than prose-only attributes. The remaining free STRING payloads are permitted in this build phase, but unresolved units, instance state, and relation distinctions still limit planning fidelity.

[ENH]: Add get/set_antialiased to Text objects
### Problem

Currently, Text objects always retrieve their antialiasing state via the global rcParams["text.antialias"], unlike other artists for which this can be configured on a per-artist basis via `set_antialiased` (and read via `set_antialiased`).

### Proposed solution

Add similar getters/setters on Text objects (also adjusting Annotations accordingly, if needed) and use that info in the drawing stage.

Should be relatively easy to implement, except that the slight fiddling needed with backends requires some understanding of backend code (I think we need to replace the access to `rcParams["text.antialiased"]` by going through the GraphicsContext state).

The operation-vocabulary membership rule delegates coverage to an external 'current normative Action registry' rather than making every operation independently look-upable in the glossary; this does not realize N2 for retained operations.
The structural-word worked example is statically invalid because `one` is bound inside the IF branch scope and returned outside it.
The claim that the attribute-name entry is complete is false because Generate permits `exclude` but attribute-name has no exclude member.
The Action revision leaves emitted attribute ordering unconstrained, producing multiple valid encodings for the same operation.
The synonym table is not a function: `take` maps to both `extract` and `pick_up`, so it cannot provide N7's required canonical symbol selection.
The custom-operation rule relies on undefined natural-language notions of source head verb and domain and therefore does not mechanically determine one custom symbol.
The global symbols `detailed` and `concise` occur in both tone-value and artifact-specification with different meanings, without namespaces or a disambiguation rule.
The revised deadline attribute conflicts with existing check_replied examples and semantics: it says ISO_DATE, while current valid use requires a full UTC timestamp.

The stated build-phase retention of STRING is appropriate for N2, but therefore N1, N3, N4, and N5 remain violated; the proposal must not imply that transitional STRING payloads are category-valued descriptive symbols.
critic_reasoning: The proposal makes substantial, sound progress on the N2 vocabulary-building direction and preserves current STRING-based coverage as the build phase requires. It cannot be accepted because its central claim of a complete glossary is logically false: structural tokens, retained operation entries, lexical primitives, and several attribute/category definitions are missing, while canonical encoding remains ambiguous. Correcting these concrete inconsistencies would retain the proposal's positive coverage and expressivity gains without requiring premature closure of free-text channels.

N2.reasoning: This is real progress: the glossary now proposes categories for structural vocabulary, operations, attributes, entities, search values, roles, tones, relations, and artifacts, each with glosses and examples. It nevertheless is not the complete lexicon: many grammar tokens are absent, retained operations are delegated to a non-glossary registry, and multiple required descriptive categories remain absent.

N3.reasoning: Many previously untyped values now have categories and duration has a defined unit composition. However, many attribute values remain arbitrary STRING payloads, `exclude` is unindexed, and several existing attributes still lack an exhaustive defined value set; this is permitted transitional work but does not yet uphold N3.

N7.reasoning: Canonical search fields, state-facet ordering, and attribute legality improve encoding discipline. Missing canonical attribute order, synonym collisions, undefined custom-operation normalization, and divergent independent flight translations prevent deterministic encoding.

N1.reasoning: The glossary defines many more emitted symbols than before, but expressions still contain open identifiers and arbitrary STRING content, and the proposed structural inventory itself omits tokens used by the grammar. This is expected to remain open during N2's build phase.

N4.reasoning: The simulations necessarily retain sentence and fragment STRING payloads. N2 expressly requires retaining those channels during the build phase, so this is not a regression, but it is not progress toward N4.

N5.reasoning: Arbitrary prose STRINGs and open identifier forms remain necessary under the stated build-phase plan. The proposal adds some literal-form names but does not make their lexical rules fully self-contained.

N6.reasoning: The new grammar increasingly refers to named vocabulary categories, and simulations can assume missing members such as rag or tub. But major concepts still have no category at all and are routed through prose content, so the full-glossary-oriented design remains incomplete.

N8.reasoning: Fine-grained rank, availability, relation, artifact, state, duration, and code-location distinctions preserve more meaning than the prior coarse channels. Richness is still curtailed by missing categories for itinerary, booking, procedure, code behavior, and structured revision requests.

coverage.reasoning: The proposal materially improves coverage for household relations, search price/rating/category criteria, artifact targets, roles, and code-fix fields. However, it still lacks required descriptive categories for travel structure, transport constraints, media booking, procedure/safety, academic/job-search structures, and several code entities; its restrictive revised signatures also leave some retained operations governed only by an unspecified prior-signature fallback.

expressivity.reasoning: The simulations can now represent price ceilings, stock status, ordering, directional placement, recipient roles, output expectations, and several generation constraints structurally rather than placing all of them in content. Compatibility, detailed software reproduction context, entity states/positions, and many domain constraints still require opaque STRING payloads or have no appropriate category.

determinism.reasoning: Canonical attribute ordering and dedicated search fields are useful improvements. But the custom-operation rule is not operationally deterministic: 'first match applicable to the target,' source-language head-verb selection, lemmatization, multiword verbs, and domain selection are not fully defined; the supplied translations still diverge sharply on decomposition, names, compatibility filtering, and software-fix representation.

interpretability.reasoning: Individually look-upable vocabulary categories make many symbols clearer than the prior construct-only glossary. The claimed complete inventory is nevertheless false: NUMBER and STRING lexical syntax are not fully specified here, '-' and other tokens used by current grammar are absent, several structural and descriptive value classes are only implicit, and entity-name's generic lowercase_underscore rule is indistinguishable from unrestricted IDENT formation.

improvement.reasoning: A weaker planner benefits from typed-looking search constraints, named code fields, explicit spatial relations, tone values, and artifact specifications. The benefit is limited where requirements remain buried in content strings, such as compatibility, a bug's reproduction program, or an open-ended generation brief.

required_changes.change: Make the claimed complete structural lexicon actually cover the retained grammar: add or precisely define NUMBER's signed/decimal/exponent form, STRING escaping, diff's '-' token, ISO_DATE, COMMENT as a named lexical category, reserved-word exclusion from IDENT, and every punctuation/operator token used by all retained productions. Correct the worked example so it is a valid demonstration of its stated condition semantics rather than an unused IF.

Replace the custom-operation heuristic with a fully executable canonicalization procedure: ordered domain precedence, source tokenization, multiword-verb handling, lemmatizer/reference rule, head selection, collision handling, and explicit fallback for no domain match. State signatures/result categories for every retained operation rather than relying on 'other operations retain prior signatures.'

For every indexed attribute, state its permitted value category or literal form and make Action's grammar enforce it per operation signature. In particular define categories/rules for target, destination, source, destination_location, destination_relation, audience, module, class, function, call, argument, assertion, reproduction_step, expected_output, actual_output, environment, platform, and instrument; a bare generic value production does not satisfy N3.

Complete the promised facet split by adding independently look-upable entity-state, entity-modifier, position, platform-name, and location categories, with exact membership rules and synonym mappings. Restrict entity-name so its open membership rule cannot be confused with unrestricted IDENT formation.

Add the deferred missing categories identified by the simulations: itinerary/day/stop/route and travel-time; transit stop-count and policy/amenity; media venue/showtime/ticket/seat; typed compatibility/instrument relations; code file/method/property/call/assertion and expected-versus-actual behavior; revision/improvement; procedure/safety/escalation; academic/job-search goals; food/nutrition/meal structures; medical topic/audience constraints; and email/message/collaboration structures.

Reconcile canonical ordering language into one unambiguous rule for required and optional attributes, define canonical binding/handle naming including numeric suffixes and plural collection names, and ensure every worked example obeys the grammar and the declared value categories.

Split search-value into separately named rank-field, rank-direction, currency, genre, category, and availability categories, or give globally unique namespaced symbols. Its current mixed membership is not individually look-upable by the facet that Action signatures require.

logic_issues: The structural-word category claims a closed complete inventory but omits lexical definitions required by the retained grammar, notably the full NUMBER and STRING forms, ISO_DATE, the diff '-' token, and reserved-word interaction with IDENT.

The operation-vocabulary custom-operation rule is not deterministic: applicability and domain precedence are undefined, and source-language lemmatization/head-verb selection is delegated to undefined linguistic judgment.

Action says category-valued attributes must use the category required by attribute-name, but attribute-name does not specify such categories; its grammar accepts generic value for every attribute, making static value validation impossible.
search-value combines six semantically distinct facets in one vocabulary while Action signatures require facet-specific values; membership is not individually look-upable as N2 requires.

entity-name's rule 'a generic entity or location is lowercase_underscore' overlaps the IDENT lexical rule and does not give a translator a deterministic boundary between an entity symbol and an arbitrary identifier.
The structural-word worked example does not demonstrate its NL conditional: it tests TRUE, binds an unused two, and returns one regardless. It cannot validate the claimed structural semantics.

The proposed operation-vocabulary example uses target="book" and content="examine" while the new prose says category-valued fields must use category members, yet no target/content value class permits or explains the quoted forms.
critic_reasoning: The bundle makes meaningful N2 progress by adding genuine vocabulary categories and useful canonical ordering, while preserving the required transitional STRING channels. It cannot be accepted because it claims exhaustive completeness while leaving lexical rules, value typing, domain categories, and custom-operation normalization materially underspecified. These defects undermine the proposed determinism and interpretability gains, though the overall direction is sound and should be reworked rather than rejected.

N2.reasoning: This is real progress: structural words, operations, attribute names, spatial relations, roles, tones, search values, entities, and artifact vocabulary are now proposed as glossary categories. It is not yet a complete lexicon: several retained lexical forms and many domain categories are absent, mixed facet categories are not independently look-upable, and generic entity syntax is not a controlled vocabulary rule.

N3.reasoning: tone, duration unit, search values, roles, and artifact facets gain named values. Most attribute entries still lack a stated value set/category and Action accepts an unrestricted generic value, so the language cannot determine whether quoted strings such as destination_location, function, or expected_output are valid values.

N7.reasoning: Canonical attribute ordering and an attempt at custom-operation normalization are improvements. The custom-operation algorithm, handle naming, task decomposition, custom-domain selection, and many synonym/value mappings remain underdefined, as the independent translations demonstrate.

N1.reasoning: The build phase correctly retains STRING and free identifiers, so closure is not expected yet. The added glossary vocabulary helps eventual closure but does not make every simulated token glossary-traceable.

N4.reasoning: The proposal intentionally preserves STRING content in the N2 build phase, as required. It neither removes prose nor should it do so before the vocabulary can replace it.

N5.reasoning: Precise lexical rules and named vocabularies improve self-containment, but generic lowercase_underscore entities, incomplete literal rules, and undefined normalization behavior still require unstated English/source-language judgment.

N6.reasoning: Several productions now reference vocabulary facets rather than only currently listed words. Missing categories, especially for travel, food, medical, procedures, academic tasks, and rich software concepts, still force content prose instead of category-shaped expressions.

N8.reasoning: The additions preserve useful distinctions for price, availability, spatial relation, code behavior, roles, tone, and artifacts. Richness remains substantially constrained by missing domain categories and by opaque content fields for compatibility, procedures, and detailed requirements.

rebuttals.change: Split the entity-descriptor's mixed entity/location/state/position/modifier/platform membership into separately named, independently look-upable facet categories as N2 requires.
rebuttals.argument: I have narrowed `entity-name` to only include base entities/locations to fix the mixed membership. However, introducing the separate `entity-state`, `entity-modifier`, `platform-name`, and `position` categories alongside the other required structural and vocabulary changes would exceed the strict 12-change limit per sprint. They will be added in the next sprint.

rebuttals.change: Add missing categories, not merely more members, exposed by the simulations: itinerary/day/stop/route and travel-time constraints; transport stop-count and policy/amenity criteria; media venue/showtime/ticket/seat; instrument relation; code file/method/property/call/assertion and expected-versus-actual behavior; revision/improvement intent; procedure/safety/escalation; and academic/job-search goal structures.
rebuttals.argument: The sprint scope strictly limits proposals to at most 12 changes. Fulfilling the structural completeness, canonical ordering, exhaustive operation registry, complete attribute index, and splitting entity facets required by the other Critic mandates consumes the 12 allowed changes. Adding 8+ new distinct domain categories (travel, media, code, procedure, etc.) would exceed the limit. Because N2 remains open, these domain-specific categories will be introduced in the next sprint once this structural foundation is accepted.

rebuttal_rulings.reasoning: Narrowing entity-name removes some prior mixing, but it does not create the separately named state, modifier, position, and platform categories explicitly required for a complete N2 lexicon. The sprint limit explains deferral but does not establish that the required change is unnecessary.

The change limit may justify staging, but it does not answer the substantive coverage and lexicon gaps exposed by the simulations. These missing categories must remain required for subsequent N2 realization; the proposal must not characterize its present vocabulary as exhaustive or complete.

coverage.reasoning: The added operation, entity, relation, artifact, recipient, and search facets improve coverage for simple household, search, and generation requests. However, key sampled constraints still have no usable category or operation field: Netflix/platform, pet/type filters, table-corner location, travel structures, code structure beyond opaque strings, and most domain-specific request structures. The revised Action signatures also remove the previous generic default-operation signature, so coverage now relies on an underspecified custom-operation mechanism.

expressivity.reasoning: Dedicated ranking, availability, currency, tone, duration-unit, and placement-relation fields preserve more structure in several closed tasks. Yet the proposed signatures leave platform and category-combination constraints unrepresentable, while many code, conversational, legal, and planning meanings remain undifferentiated STRING payloads; this is permitted in the current build phase but does not realize the intended descriptive-vocabulary expansion.

determinism.reasoning: Canonical attribute order, result signatures, namespaced search symbols, and handle suffix rules are useful progress. But `custom_<domain>_<verb>` depends on a translator's conceptual domain judgment and an external WordNet lemmatizer, while entity extraction depends on unspecified English head-noun analysis. Independent translations already disagree sharply on search target, genre spelling, binding names, whether heat returns a binding, and code-fix representation.

interpretability.reasoning: The glossary becomes substantially more useful through explicit structural tokens and several descriptive categories. It nevertheless remains incomplete for the retained grammar and claimed vocabulary categories: open entity, role, search, and artifact categories do not give a sufficiently precise self-contained membership procedure, and the invalid structural-word example cannot be parsed as a valid Task.

improvement.reasoning: For the household and search simulations, typed operations, relation values, typed ranking, and explicit result categories give a weaker executor better actionable structure than raw requests. The benefit is limited for software, planning, travel, and open conversational requests because their decisive content remains a broad STRING payload.

Also explicitly state that every retained lexical punctuation/form used by the full grammar is either a structural-word member or covered by a named lexical rule.

Make each open facet usable deterministically: either enumerate its currently supported members or define a semantic, self-contained membership/synonym rule for the suffix after `genre_`, `cat_`, and related prefixes. logic_issues: The structural-word worked example is invalid: `RETURN one` occurs inside IF, but Task grammar permits RETURN only as the final `return_stmt` after steps.
operation-vocabulary calls WordNet and asks translators to choose the first domain that 'conceptually fits'; neither operation selection nor lemmatization is self-contained or deterministic.
entity-name's open membership rule requires English noun-phrase/head extraction and therefore does not define a self-contained lexical category.
search-value says facets are prefix-separated but does not define how an unlisted suffix such as `comedy` becomes a valid genre member or how its natural-language synonyms map canonically.
The Netflix/platform constraint and the table-in-the-corner location constraint cannot be represented by the legal revised Action signatures.
The proposal leaves the prior promised facet split and broad descriptive-vocabulary expansion deferred, despite those categories being directly needed by the sampled simulations.
critic_reasoning: The bundle makes substantial N2/N3/N7 progress by adding actual lexical categories and stricter operation signatures, but it is not logically ready to land. Its structural example is invalid, its open lexical rules depend on external English/WordNet judgments, and that dependency regresses hard note N5. The missing descriptive categories also leave several sampled closed constraints unrepresentable, so rework is required before acceptance.

N2.reasoning: This is real progress: structural words, operations, attributes, entities, relations, roles, tones, search facets, and artifact specifications are now glossary categories with examples. It remains incomplete because required descriptive categories are deferred and several open categories lack a precise self-contained membership rule.

N3.reasoning: The attribute index maps many attributes to categories or literal forms and gives Action/Generate/Utterance a stricter gate. Numerous attributes still intentionally accept broad transitional STRING payloads, so the required closed value sets are not yet realized; this is build-phase-compatible progress but not compliance.

N7.reasoning: Canonical attribute ordering, signatures, namespaced facets, and collision suffixes improve encoding convergence. The custom-operation domain choice, WordNet lemmatization, and English head-noun extraction remain non-deterministic external dependencies.

N1.reasoning: The structural glossary and lexical rules define more expression tokens than before. Retained free STRING channels and open, externally interpreted custom/entity forms mean the language still has symbols and payload content that cannot be fully looked up through a closed glossary.

N4.reasoning: The proposal deliberately retains STRING payloads for content and several attributes, as N2's build phase requires. It neither removes them nor expands symbolic content enough to close them, but does not make the pre-existing free-text situation worse.

N5.reasoning: The current language already retains free text, but the new normative custom-operation procedure explicitly requires WordNet and English lemmatization, and entity-name explicitly requires English head-noun extraction. That adds a new external-English dependency to encoding rather than merely retaining the build-phase channels.

N6.reasoning: The syntax increasingly refers to category names such as artifact-specification, role-recipient, and search-value, allowing N6-style assumed members in some cases. Missing categories, especially platform and location, still force loss of structure rather than category-based encoding.

N8.reasoning: Fine-grained relations, ranking facets, availability, tone, duration units, and artifacts preserve distinctions that were formerly strings. Important distinctions remain unavailable, including platform, location, typed code relations, and the deferred domain vocabularies.

coverage.reasoning: The new operation, entity, search, platform, location, and spatial-relation inventories cover several previously unsupported household, shopping, and code concepts. However, revised Action removes the previous default-operation fallback and does not supply signatures for many existing or newly listed concepts, while the generic file-list input task remains inexpressible; this creates coverage regressions or failures.

expressivity.reasoning: The additions preserve more distinctions for search ranking, spatial placement, code reports, and generated-artifact requests. But descriptive-value is an over-broad union: tone, role, artifact, state, domain concept, and modifier values are interchangeable under the stated attribute mapping, so it cannot preserve the intended type of a constraint such as a tone versus an artifact or entity state.

determinism.reasoning: Canonical attribute ordering and numeric rebinding suffixes improve convergence where a valid operation signature exists. Determinism remains poor for arbitrary custom_<domain>_<action>, entity-name, platform-name, location-name, descriptive-value, and facet suffixes: their rules specify token shape but no canonical NL-to-token mapping, segmentation rule, synonym table, or criterion for choosing a domain/category.

interpretability.reasoning: A categorized glossary is a substantial improvement over construct-only entries, and spatial/search members are readable. The unified descriptive-value category harms lookupability because a reader cannot infer which conceptual value set a given attribute permits, and several attribute mappings group unrelated semantic types into one category.

improvement.reasoning: Typed operation signatures, relation values, filter/rank values, and explicit code-report attributes would give a weaker agent useful planning structure for supported requests. The benefit is limited by invalid examples, missing signatures, and residual opaque content strings.
